text:
maya: quick async check-in — midday. What I did: reviewed the latest spec for adaptive routing, validated acceptance criteria with eng. Blockers: wondering if we should reduce scope for v1 to avoid adding cross-region failover. Today: want a final call on scope + sign-off or a prioritized backlog of follow-ups.

alex: what I did: pushed PR #4567 that wires the routing policy into the canary config, added unit tests. Blockers: CI flake on the `kv-cache` integration test — looks like a race in the mock. Today: will debug the test and try to get the PR green; if not, request a manual canary.

maya: @alex thanks — if you need a manual canary, ping infra and I'll coordinate stakeholder heads-up. For scope: proposal is to ship without cross-region failover (capture as follow-up) and keep single-region fallback to smaller model variants. Thoughts?

sanjay: what I did: validated Dedicated capacity profiles in staging; found a throughput regression (~8%) when we enable continuous batching plus quantization on the A100 pool. Blockers: need to profile kernel selection to see if it's falling back to unoptimized kernels. Today: will run perf traces and open an infra ticket with logs.

tori: what I did: updated the UX acceptance criteria to include explicit error messaging for model fallback and added metrics to the checklist. Blockers: waiting on the final error strings from eng. Today: will draft the copy once we have the messages.

maya: quick prioritization note — since Dedicated customers expect predictable latency, the throughput regression sounds higher priority than cross-region. Proposal: 1) delay cross-region feature to next sprint, 2) prioritize infra perf work + a canary showing latency meets SLOs.

alex: agree with prioritization. If sanjay can isolate the kernel fallback case today I can add a guard in the runtime to force the optimized path for the canary. That should unblock the SLA risk.

sanjay: will try to reproduce in staging by 3pm PST and tag @alex in the ticket. If we need to, we can cut a manual canary using Dedicated pool `dc-manual-canary-v3`.

meredith: quick design note — if we do the manual canary, can we flag the console UI with a banner: "Manual canary in progress — expect increased error rates"? I can supply copy + severity level.

maya: yes please; meredith if you drop the copy here I will include it in the stakeholder email. Also @tori do you want to keep the UX ACs for fallback errors in the v1 checklist or move to follow-up?

tori: keep them in v1 but mark them "graceful degradation only". We'll accept simplified messaging for now and iterate post-launch.

deploy-bot: deploy request received — manual canary `dc-manual-canary-v3` scheduled at 2024-07-12T20:00:00Z by maya. (reacts :rocket:)

alex: acked the deploy. FYI I've added a small smoke test to PR #4567: ```bash
make smoke-test TARGET=dc-manual-canary-v3
```

maya: next steps: sanjay will post perf ticket link here when ready, alex will try the guarded runtime change if needed, meredith will post banner copy, tori keeps UX ACs in v1 with reduced scope. If nothing blocks the manual canary tonight I'll send the stakeholder note at 18:30 PST. :thumbsup:

sanjay: posted perf ticket: https://internal/repo/issues/7891 — logs and perf traces uploaded. I put an initial hypothesis in the ticket; tagging @alex.

alex: taking a look now. If I can't isolate within an hour I'll open a short RFC for the guard and request an expedited review.

maya: thanks team — will follow up after the canary run. If anyone hits a blocker call out here and I'll pull in support.

(reacts: maya :eyes:, alex :thumbsup:, meredith :rocket:)
